newsitem.title: USA: Lawmakers offer bill to ban clearcut in US forests.
newsitem.headline: Lawmakers offer bill to ban clearcut in US forests.

text.p: Clearcut logging in federal forests would be banned under legislation unveiled Thursday in the U.S. House.

Democratic Reps. Anna Eshoo of California and Carolyn Maloney of New York introduced the bill, which also would make conservation and restoration of native biodiversity the priority of federal forest management and would ban logging and roadbuilding in ancient forests of the Northwest.

The bill also would bar systematic logging of trees that are the same age on federal lands, bar logging and roadbuilding in roadless areas and in specially designated areas deemed valuable as watersheds, for recreation, endangered species habitat, or for old-growth trees.
Eshoo at a news conference said the bill already had more than 50 sponsors and she hoped to gain broad enough support to force the committees with jurisdiction to hold hearings on the bill.

"That's tough sledding, I know," she said, as the chairmen of the House Resources Committee and the Agriculture Committee have pushed policies to encourage more logging of federal forests. Eshoo also said a companion bill will be offered in the Senate.
